ops.title: v0.55.1 \"stabilize file provider launches\" REMOVED the v0.55.0 shallow-per-tick FP heal cadence (it woke appexes → launch storm); the healer is now deep-only. Do not re-add shallow-per-tick.
ops.body:
The v0.55.0 EDEADLK train SPLIT the File Provider heal into a cheap shallow probe every healer tick + a deep probe every 5 min (fp.domain deep lane + fp.shallow debounce lane). **v0.55.1 "stabilize file provider launches" (commit d80d69b8) reversed that split** — the rationale is in `internal/daemon/fpheal.go` (the healthy-domain arm): *"Even the companion app's shallow enumeration wakes an appex, so running it on every healer tick creates a fleet-wide launch storm."* The shallow-per-tick was itself re-triggering the appex launch storm the v0.55.0 work was meant to kill. The healer is now **deep-only**: healthy domains get the slow `fpDeepProbe` on `fpDeepProbeInterval`; parked/wedged re-probe deep on their own schedules. The `fp.shallow` ledger policy was deleted as dead. **Do not re-introduce a shallow probe on the healer tick.** The `ProbeDomainShallow` op still exists and is fine for ONE-SHOT user-initiated use (doctor daemon-down path, `internal/cli/service.go`) — the storm was per-tick, not the op itself.

Companion commit 2bc66c89 "propagate daemon operation contexts" added `Manager.SyncOverlayContext` — a launch-bound, ctx-aware sync (via `contextOverlaySyncer`/`syncFileProviderContext`) so FP control calls at launch carry the real op ctx, not the provider's background context. It is the LAUNCH path (`internal/cli/select.go`), lease-protected — distinct from the background-poll `SyncOverlay` (`scheduler.go`), which is where the remove-vs-poll GetAccount-recheck guard belongs (a guard on SyncOverlayContext would be redundant).

**cc-pool v0.56.0** (merge 18957cc2, tag 2026-07-16) landed the FP bridge data-plane verdict train ON TOP of v0.55.1: fusekit **v1.2.0** (`content.BridgeClient.SelfTest` round-trip health check, `fileproviderd.ErrAppDialRefused` dial-refusal subset, exported `proc.Flock`) + the bridge verdict (`FPBridgeVerdict` serving/consent-parked/bound-dead/down, `fp.bridge` ledger row, `OpFPBridgeCheck`, doctor renders the verdict), the `ccp fp consent` lever (TCC-probe exec'd from the stable binary with lstat+owner+O_NOFOLLOW hardening, version-skew guard, SSH refusal), the needs-login classifier fix (`creds.ErrNotFound`→`ErrNeedsLogin` in `ensureFreshToken` only) + auth_health gen-CAS TOCTOU fix, and a small-fix sweep (ensureFPAppAsync race, stale companion-app reap, SyncOverlay remove-guard, FinalizeAdd atomicity, flock consumption). Main bumped `ProtocolVersion` 1→2 (coordinated with the widget's `supportedProto`) — the StatusSnapshot `proto` field shares that constant and the widget hard-rejects a mismatch, so never bump it without the widget.

Transcript-archaeology gotcha: the parallel session's cc-notes and plan files are git-synced and injected into EVERY session's context, so keyword search across transcripts matches all ~119 cc-pool sessions identically — you cannot isolate an authoring session by grepping shared terms. jj-authored commits also don't appear as Bash tool calls. The authoritative "why" for such changes is the code the commit produced, not the transcript.

Related: [[fp-edeadlk-v0550-train]], [[yasyf-home-fp-bridge-outage-retreat]].
